content.text: {"headline":"Approve P3: full response with overtime. It is the only plan that reaches the 80% target, at an extra cost of ₹15,840.","why":"Payments calls are running up to 72% above forecast (112 vs 65 at 09:15). The rise most likely comes from the 08:35 UPI cashback push, MKT-2026-409, sent to 1.2M app users. Confidence in that cause is medium, because the 08:00 bump came before the push. Staffing is normal, so this is a demand spike, not an attendance problem. With no action, service level for 09:30–14:15 drops to 34.7% (payments 16.2%) and abandons reach 19.2%. P3 combines overtime (25 payments agents 10:00–12:00, 20 agents 12:00–14:00), an IVR message and chat deflection for refund/payment-status/UPI-failure calls, IVR callback, and a 45-minute delay to breaks. Predicted results: 91.1% service level (payments 92.2%, general 89.4%), 2.5% abandons, and 93.7% for the rest of the day. It has no policy violations.","trade_offs":["P1 (no cost) does almost nothing: 35.1% service level and 17.2% abandons.","P2 costs only ₹2,880 but falls short at 71.4% (payments 64.7%). It is the fallback if overtime take-up is poor.","P4 costs more than P3 (₹16,524) and only reaches 77.4%, because it drops the IVR message and callback. Its one advantage is less friction for customers in the IVR.","P3 means customers hear an IVR message and are pushed towards chat and callbacks. The general queue improves under P3 (89.4% vs 75.2% with no action), so there is no risk to it.","There is no escalation flag, but ₹15,840 is the largest spend that meets the target."],"watch":"Check overtime acceptance by 10:00. If fewer agents accept than offered, the result moves towards P2's 71%. Track payments volume against the 112-per-interval peak, and check whether refund_status, upi_payment_failed and payment_status_enquiry calls ease off. If they don't, the campaign link may be wrong and the volume could persist past 14:15."}
